text: And I think we can consider how best to rehabilitate him and keep working on ensuring that "we come together as a nation with a view to sporting excellence".

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: Will the Member join me in supporting him?

speaker: Mdm Deputy Speaker
text: We just need to move the Exempted Business Motion so that we can continue with the Motion.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: But let me start by assuring the House that regular and consistent review and evaluation are conducted as part and parcel of our High-Performance Sports (HPS) ecosystem.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Through our review, we examine: (a) what has worked, (b) what has not worked, (c) what we could do differently and (d) chart our future priorities.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: But we must accurately define what “winning” is.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: While recognising that we cannot compete directly with countries that have large populations, we have also performed well in many sports, including swimming, sailing, table tennis, badminton, silat – just to name a few.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Assoc Prof Jamus Lim distributed a handout suggesting that GDP per capita spending is a predictor of sporting success.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: First, I wish to point out that the handout does not attribute what the data sources are.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Second, saying that sporting success can be pinned down to one predictor is perhaps overly simplistic and shows a lack of understanding of the complexity of our sporting endeavour.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: In fact, the scatter plot provided by Assoc Prof Jamus Lim himself substantiates the point that perhaps there is no correlation between spending and achievement, given the spread of the data points.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Many more factors are at play, depending on the operating context across countries, and this should also not be limited to just medals, because they are just the tip of the iceberg.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Instead, we focus on the development of the sport ecosystem and support systems – a journey that may take an athlete eight to 12 years – to get athletes to the peak of their performance, to realise their full potential, often at a major games or major championships, against the best in Asia or the world.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: The book, Project 0812, encapsulates this belief, highlighting how our achievements at the Olympics were 20 years or more in the making.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Our basis is the well-researched and internationally recognised SPLISS model.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: SPLISS stands for “Sports Policy Factors Leading to International Sporting Success”.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: This model focuses on key components that make up successful sports ecosystems.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: In this model, researchers identified nine pillars underpinned by 96 critical success factors that successful sporting nations exhibit.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: This model has helped us review existing high-performance infrastructure as well as identify gaps and determine priorities for infrastructure development on a sport-by-sport basis.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: And we have seen results of these efforts.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Bowler Shayna Ng clinched the International Bowling Federation Super World Championships Women’s Single Title in 2021.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: She is also Chair of SNOC's Athletes’ Commission, representing and advocating for our athletes.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Silat athlete Sheik Farhan secured his fourth World Championship Title at the 19th World Pencak Silat Championships in 2022.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Farhan also clinched the Singapore Youth Award in 2019 and was also the first Silat exponent to make the Forbes “30 Under 30 Asia” list.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Particularly significant were the PBs, podium finish or otherwise.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: These are powerful testimonies of our athletes striving to be the best sporting versions of themselves.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: After all, it is not just about winning medals, as hon Member He Ting Ru has mentioned in her speech as well.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: As Australian Olympic swimmer and gold medallist Bronte Barratt puts it, it is about trying to win.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: The motto is "faster, higher, stronger”; not “fastest, highest, strongest”.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Our youths and debutants, too, did us proud.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: As Ms Poh Li San mentioned, Izaac Quek swept all the table tennis men’s events, winning all three golds in singles, doubles and team.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Swimmer Nicholas Mahabir also performed spectacularly, winning two golds in the relay events as well as three individual silvers.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: And it is perhaps worth noting that Izaac was just 16 at the time and Nicholas 18.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Swimmer Colin Soon not only won four golds and one silver but also shattered four Games and national records.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: These achievements were only possible because of the “village” behind our TeamSG athletes.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Family members, caregivers and friends whose enduring love, sacrifice and belief gave our athletes the strength to turn dreams into reality, something that Member Ms Sylvia Lim is very familiar with.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Coaches, for investing time and energy and being role models for our athletes; coach Roland, along with Lionel Leong and Ang Peng Siong, have been instrumental in our swimmers’ journey and I was glad that we were able to get Roland that opportunity to present a medal to Colin, his last gold medal.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: And you can feel and see for yourself that exhilaration on Roland’s face.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: And not forgetting our sports associations and councils, chefs de missions, corporates, Team Nila volunteers and fans who were a constant source of support for our athletes.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: In the next half an hour or so, I want to bring Members into a time warp by illustrating the support that our HPS systems provide through the lens and “life course” of a hypothetical young boy, five-year-old Samuel.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: To be clear, the boy is hypothetical but the programmes and policies are real.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Samuel and his family live in a HDB flat with an open-air hardcourt downstairs.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Noticing his love for sports, Samuel’s parents considered a range of options for him to explore his interests – sports co-curricular activities (CCAs) in schools, ActiveSG programmes, private academies and clubs as well as private coaching.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: The parents signed Samuel up for programmes run by ActiveSG academies and clubs, whose variety meant Samuel tried out different sports at a very young age.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Samuel’s parents gladly utilised ActiveSG credits that have been provided since 2014, not knowing that these credits probably helped raise sports participation among Singaporeans from 54% in 2015 to some 74% in 2022.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: And this was driven by our belief that grassroots participation and high performance are not at odds.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: In fact, they go hand in hand as part of our sporting ecosystem.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: At Primary 4, Samuel’s teacher nominates him to go for the Junior Sports Academy (JSA) selection trials, a collaboration between the Ministry of Education (MOE) and the National Youth Sports Institute (NYSI).

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Under this programme, primary school students like Samuel with higher abilities in the physical domain try out different sports and identify where their talent and passion lie.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Samuel has lots of fun playing four different sports and, during the programme, he discovers his love for badminton.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: In the JSA programme, Samuel meets Syahbil and understands that Syahbil was exposed to sports through the SportCares Saturday Night Lights football programme, one of several programmes that provide bursaries for children that come from low-income families to learn a sport.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Samuel is particularly inspired by Syahbil as he also goes the extra mile to help others in need and give back actively by volunteering through SportCares.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: As their friendship develops, Samuel looks for opportunities to play badminton with Syahbil outside of school and outside of the JSA.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Samuel looks forward to the upcoming sporting facilities that will be built around his neighbourhood.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: And Samuel is particularly excited about the Toa Payoh Integrated Development (TPID) because it is near home and he knows that there will be many more badminton courts.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: And he has high hopes for the facility because he had visited Bukit Canberra before.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Bukit Canberra featured facilities, such as indoor sports halls, swimming pools, gyms, fitness studios, a hawker centre and a polyclinic.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: And Samuel has also heard from his friends about the Sport-in-Precinct facilities in Nee Soon Central, Woodlands and Gek Poh as well as the rejuvenation works that were done to the Delta and Choa Chu Kang Sport Centres.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Soon, the Primary School Leaving Examination (PSLE) looms ahead but Samuel is thrilled to join the Singapore Sports School (SSP) via the Direct School Admission (DSA).

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: In Samuel’s mind, SSP is where he can pursue both sporting and academic excellence.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Today, SSP has 10 academies, such as shooting as well as individual programmes that accept students from other sports, such as wushu.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Past and present student-athletes have also performed well at Major Games and Championships.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: They also accounted for about 30% of the medals and gold medals won by Team Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: On the academic front, SSP students had also done well – 67% of student-athletes scored at least 40 points out of the maximum 45 points for IB exams while more than 95% of the GCE “O” level cohort qualified for junior college or polytechnic courses.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: SSP also takes care of athletes’ life issues, for instance, providing education and counselling guidance.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Samuel’s friends have also shared with him about fellow SSP student-athlete, fencer Juliet Heng – a real person, by the way – who had done an excellent job of balancing her academic pursuits with her sporting ambitions.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Like Samuel, Juliet came through the JSA in 2015, where she participated in four sports, including fencing.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Juliet then took up SSP’s Learn-to-Fence programme in January 2017 and joined SSP’s fencing academy the year after.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Progressing over the years, Juliet qualified for the Asian and World Cadets and Juniors Fencing Championships in 2021.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: She was youth-carded in 2022, placing her on the high-performance pathway as a junior athlete.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: As a result of her youth-carding, Juliet received funding support which fully subsidised her participation in local and overseas competitions and facilitated her development as an athlete.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Juliet fenced her way to the top 32 at the 2022 World Fencing Championships and quickly became a spexScholar in 2023.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: As a spexScholar, Juliet received increased support, opening doors to greater opportunities, including partaking in more than eight International Fencing Federation competitions and overseas training camps with other top-tier fencers, which contributed to her ascent in the world rankings.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Juliet was also provided comprehensive assistance, including tailored programmes in areas, such as strength and conditioning, psychology, biomechanics, nutrition and many other essential elements, that contribute to her holistic growth as an athlete.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Back to Samuel, who has since joined the Singapore Sports School, displaying several strong performances in youth-level competitions.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: However, he finds the transition from youth-level competitions to senior tournaments challenging.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Nevertheless, Samuel presses on, drawing encouragement from sport climber Luke Goh who similarly recognised the difficulty of youth-to-senior transitions, where "everyone's mindset and mentality just got more cut-throat and intense".

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: But yet, Luke scaled that transition to secure a bronze medal at the 2022 International Federation of Sport Climbing Asian Cup.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Luke was also, coincidentally, one of the first youth athletes whom I had met when I first took on the role of Parliamentary Secretary at MCCY.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Luke's steely resolve to shine at sport climbing, even at a young age then, left a deep impression on me.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: He is a perfect example of how NYSI has been supporting emerging sports, such as sport climbing, bicycle motocross (BMX) and skateboarding.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Samuel has since graduated from SSP and has enlisted into NS.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: He is grateful that since this year, spexScholars are allowed to retain their scholarship while serving NS as well as have existing provisions to support their training and preparation of our national athletes, taking into account the specific circumstances of the athlete, his sport, subject to the SAF and Home Team's operational requirements.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Samuel met Team Singapore hurdler Ang Chen Xiang, who gives him confidence to do well both in sport and in NS.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: It was challenging, to say the least, for Chen Xiang, having to manage training and competitions alongside heavy commitments as a medical officer in the First Commando Battalion.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Yet, Chen Xiang clinched the silver medal in the men's 110 metres hurdles final at the 31st SEA Games last year while serving NS.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: He continued to deliver a stunning performance at this year's SEA Games after he "ORD-ed", clinching a gold medal in the same event – as the first Singaporean champion in the event since 1967.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Chen Xiang credits his performance to his fellow medical officers who had covered his duties when he was away for competition.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: This gives Samuel quiet confidence that his colleagues will be equally supportive.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Samuel has since "ORD-ed", balancing university with his sporting ambitions.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: That has not been easy, but Samuel is glad, however, that the spexEducation scheme helps him to juggle sports and education by supporting him with school admissions, scholarships and scheduling his classes around training and competitions.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Samuel knows that he will soon need to balance his sporting pursuits not with studies but with his work commitments.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Samuel is also glad that he can train at the Singapore Sports Hub that has really blossomed into a vibrant sporting and lifestyle precinct for athletes and the general community alike.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: The National School Games Finals at the Sports Hub are now a common affair and it warms Samuel's heart to see inter-generational families spending their evenings and weekends enjoying community programmes at the Sports Hub.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: He also looks forward to competing for a medal at the Sports Hub in his maiden participation in the Singapore Badminton Open, a Super 750 event that has made Singapore one of the most prestigious spots on the Badminton World Federation (BWF) World Tour, only behind the World Tour Finals and the four Super 1000 tournaments.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Samuel loves the challenge and he knows he has home ground support.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Samuel is now an aspiring Olympian and receives an even larger tranche of support as compared to when he was younger.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: This mirrors the support that shuttler Loh Kean Yew receives today, including annual grants that provide access, including but not limited to technical directors, coaches, National Training Centres and tailored sports science and sports medicine support.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: After the Tokyo Olympics in 2021, Kean Yew was invited to train with Viktor Axelsen in Dubai.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Singapore Sport Institute's (SSI) Athlete Life Team also provided education counselling to Kean Yew when he was studying in Republic Polytechnic and when he decided to pursue badminton full-time.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: With the weight of the nation's expectation on Samuel, he is slowly feeling the pressure.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Social media is abuzz with scathing scrutiny of his performance.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Online kerfuffle between loyal fans and naysayers fuel unnecessary speculations and judgement.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: If only someone could share with Samuel that years before, Kean Yew experienced the same pressures.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Earlier last month, I met Kean Yew on the sidelines of the Singapore Open.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: He had just exited in the second round but he was, as usual, looking cheery when I met him.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: After chatting with our shuttlers, I pulled Kean Yew aside.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: I checked in with him on his mental state and well-being, something that I have always been concerned about.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: I spoke to Kean Yew again last night over the phone to seek his consent for my sharing in this Chamber.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Because what was apparent to me then from that conversation was that the weight of an entire nation's expectations was squarely on this young man's shoulders and he was fully aware of that.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: And I raise this today in the hope that all of us can be that little bit more sensitive and that little bit more supportive.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Athletes want to live up to fans' expectations but fans need to understand that athletes, too, are human.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Let us not forget that it is not all just about medals, but rather, it is about journeying with our athletes as they work through their daily struggles in realising their maximal potential.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: While the pressure overwhelms him at times, Samuel is encouraged by his friends.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: However, not all is a bed of roses.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: In the gripping quarter finals against the world No 3, Samuel eventually succumbs in his first Olympic endeavour.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: As Samuel marches to the back of house, holding back tears, his coach says to him, "Sport is not merely about the medals.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: It is about training to be the best version of yourself.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: You have done yourself and Singapore proud." These words spur Samuel on as he starts again for the next Olympic cycle – his window to perform.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Training is tough but, against all odds, Samuel prevails, winning a silver medal at the following Olympics.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Remembering Olympic figure skater Michelle Kwan's wisdom, Samuel says in a post-match interview, "I didn't lose the gold.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: We also note Ms Sylvia Lim's proposal on post-retirement medical support.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: To give back to the sport and community, Samuel decides to take on coaching roles within the Singapore Badminton Association (SBA) to nurture and inspire the next generation of shuttlers.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: As a retired athlete who makes sustained contributions to the sport and the community after retirement, he has been nominated and will likely qualify for induction into the Singapore Sport Hall of Fame.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: He will join the ranks of almost 60 other athletes, including track superstar C Kunalan, bowler Remy Ong and swimmer Theresa Goh.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Some of these retired athletes have, in turn, been invited to provide their views on Hall of Fame nominees.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: His coach, too, has been included in the Hall of Fame under the category for Sports Leaders that had been created to honour the contribution of sports administrators, coaches and scientists, amongst others.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: With the Government's review of the Sports Excellence (spex) Framework, we hope that there will be more "Samuels" to come.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: One of these revisions was extending the spexScholarships in 2022 beyond just athletes competing in major games to our very own world indoor skydiving champion, Kyra Poh.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: We will also continue to facilitate and provide some access to gym facilities, sport psychologists as well as training and competition facilities for our athletes in emerging, new and niche sports.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: As we continue to scale up support for our athletes, I would like to assure this House that the Government will do likewise for our current and next generation of para-athletes.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Our para-athletes have been an inspiration to all of us, showing what it means to not be defined or constrained by physical limits.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: One such example is para-powerlifter Nur Aini, who, at the 2017 ASEAN Para Games, was the first Singaporean woman to compete in para-powerlifting.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Across several major games, Aini made steady progress but was beset by an injury following the 2022 Paralympics.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: This injury required surgery, but Aini remained unfazed and persevered to compete in the 2022 Commonwealth Games.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: We also have a team of dedicated SSI sports scientists who have been doggedly considering ways for our para-athletes to further maximise their potential.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Aini and Diroy are just some examples out of numerous para-athletes – or as I prefer to say, athletes – who have represented Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Each of these athletes empower persons with disabilities to live better through sports, exemplifying how sports can reduce the stigma and discrimination sometimes associated with disability.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: That is why the Government has been and will continue to invest resources in promoting disability sports.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: I assure Ms He Ting Ru that this figure cited in the Enabling Masterplan is based on Sport Singapore's National Sport Participation Survey, so they are fully aligned and accurate.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: The Government will continue to better support disability sports.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Even as the Government continues to support our athletes, I urge corporates and Members of this House to partner us.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: I spoke earlier about how it takes a village to raise an athlete and I hope, sincerely, that as a nation, we can continue to grow this village.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: I thus urge that all of us use our platforms to be cheerleaders for our athletes, whether they win or lose.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: And I echo Mr Mark Chay and Ms Poh Li San who called on corporates to support our athletes and I would like to suggest two ways for corporates to help.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: This can be through donations to the One Team Singapore Fund (OTSF), which will support our athletes in enhancing their training environments and in increasing competition opportunities.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: One such beneficiary was the Singapore Floorball Association, who had used OTSF to subsidise their overseas training and competition costs.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: This exposed our floorball athletes to a higher level of international competitive floorball, where our Singapore Under-19 men's team managed to participate in the 12th men's Under-19 World Floorball Championships in April 2023.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Second, by joining the spexBusiness network to help support current and former TeamSG athletes in pursuing meaningful careers while balancing their sporting commitments.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: As we have heard from Samuel's story, many of these have already been implemented and those not implemented may or may not be practical or does not really account for our context.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: But I just want to assure Members of this House that we are always improving the system and we welcome all Singaporeans to support us in this journey because this journey in creating sporting success needs partnerships.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: At this juncture, I would also like to take some time to respond to some of the points that had been raised.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: On football, Goal 2034 is a project aimed at galvanising improvements to our football standards at all levels and paying particular attention to the base.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: This requires a whole-of-society approach for all of us to get behind these efforts.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: We have outlined this approach on several occasions.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Do we want to qualify for the World Cup?

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Every country serious about sports will want to aspire towards that.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: But it is more important for us to be focused on building sustainable, long-lasting foundations to anchor our sporting aspirations, including football.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: On the Sports Hub, we have made various statements on the termination sum and I will not go into details on this.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: This is a Motion on sports not on Public-Private Partnership (PPP), and let us focus on that.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: In any case, as Member Assoc Prof Jamus Lim has acknowledged, Minister Edwin Tong has already covered the takeover of Sports Hub in detail during his Ministerial Statement last year.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: In gist, we went for a PPP due to the international private sector expertise we could tap on and the lack of upfront capital costs from the Government.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: And when our partners fell short, we made a decision to terminate and we got a fair deal.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: This was also laid out in February this year.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: It has only been a short period of time since we took back the Sports Hub in December last year.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: We have also built a healthy pipeline of world-class, not just entertainment, but also sporting events.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: So, besides concerts, we have marquee sports events taking place or have not already taken place in the Sports Hub, such as Rugby Sevens, Singapore Smash, Singapore Badminton Open, the FIBA Intercontinental Cup and the FIBA 3X3 Asia Cup.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: On emerging sports, we need to make optimal use of our limited resources.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Our priority and, hence, our investment, is channelled to developing a sustained pipeline of athletes to represent our nation at elite competitions, including major games.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: We are, nevertheless, looking at more ways to support athletes in new, emerging and niche sports.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: On broadcast, the broadcasting of sports competitions is a useful platform to promote the efforts of Team Singapore athletes and drive greater support for Team Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Mediacorp broadcasts a range of sporting competitions and events on its free-to-air channels and meWATCH.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: But decisions related to sports broadcasting really depends on several considerations, including things like time zone, media rights, audience interest.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: So, I hope the Member who raised these points can appreciate these complexities.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: When I started, I spoke about regular and consistent review and evaluation being part and parcel of our HPS ecosystem, regardless of this or any other Motion.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Our goals in sport will not solely be our medal count.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Rather, ingredients that will allow us to build a successful HPS ecosystem.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: We will also continue to enhance access to sporting facilities through our Sports Facilities Master Plan.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: But as a nation, all of us must rally behind our athletes, regardless of whether they win or lose.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Why we continue to invest in sport is because of its ability to rally communities together and foster national pride and cohesion.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Take, for example, the Suzuki Cup semi-finals two years back on Boxing Day where our Lions lost the match to Indonesia while three men down, but won the hearts of all Singaporeans.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: The immense pride that we all felt, that I felt, when Majulah Singapura filled the National Stadium that evening.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: But it is only possible if we come together as a nation to support our athletes, regardless of outcome.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: No doubt, Singapore is a little red dot.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: But we have time and again shown the world what we are made of.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
text: I had originally thought we would end by 6.00 pm which perhaps points to my own naive optimism and, contrary to the text of the Motion, in my inability to set achievable goals.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
text: As the many varied and charged speeches from both sides of the House as well as among our NMP ranks, delivered over the course of this Motion, attest, sport actually has a remarkable ability to excite, inspire and unite.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
text: It also has an incredible ability to foster euphoria as well as despair.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
text: I recall how I remained on cloud nine a good week after the Golden State Warriors, my favourite basketball team, won the National Basketball Association (NBA) finals last year.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
text: But I also felt an annoying sense of loss when, back in May, I watched my alma mater's "A" division rugby team lose in the final minutes to an arch rival.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
text: Others will undoubtedly share how they felt after the Young Lions' 7-0 thrashing by Malaysia that same month.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
text: And this notion that sports can and do contribute to national well-being is not just a vague hypothesis.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
text: And as He Ting Ru has pointed out in her speech, there are clear biological pathways for why sports contribute not just to physical but also mental well-being.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
text: The sentiment was also echoed by Sylvia Lim and Xie Yao Quan.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
text: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary went through a slate of examples for how the Government's sports programmes have helped individual athletes who, in turn, have gone on to succeed in these sporting endeavours.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
text: We have, to be clear, zero quarrel with these and, indeed, congratulate both the sportsmen and women who have won sporting medals and, often, with impressive academic results to boot.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
text: We do not even doubt that Government support has been instrumental in their success.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
text: But once again, the proof of the pudding is in the eating and the question we ask is: what of those who did not find success?

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
text: The examples that he cites often smell of selection bias and we are left to wonder what could have happened.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
text: For our level of income and what we spend, why is it that we underperform as a nation?

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
text: I should clarify at this point perhaps that the source of the charts that I used and circulated was, well, myself, two hours on a Sunday afternoon, based on publicly available data on FIFA rankings, Olympic medals and GDP per capita.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
text: And of course, I am well aware that sports performance depends on much more than income.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
text: But I came to the conclusion that they have all come to the same conclusion as I have.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
text: I shared the charts because I thought that they conveyed the point much more cleanly and much more clearly than the suite of references would.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
text: As a political officeholder, I am sure Senior Parliamentary Secretary Chua would appreciate the value of a message simply conveyed.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
text: Singaporeans have been starved of the opportunity to cheer their national athletes even more than they have been able to.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
text: So, to be clear, we are not disparaging our current athletes or when they inevitably stumble now and then and do not medal.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
text: That is right in the Motion, not just for medals, but their accomplishments, which include even qualifying for the games in the first place.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
text: But the Motion is asking – indeed, pleading – on behalf of all Singaporeans, for these successful athletes we have yet to see.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
text: Member Wan Rizal explained that sporting success is also manifold and felt that the text of the Motion did not sufficiently capture this aspect.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
text: I am afraid I have to disagree with this one.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
text: Indeed, both Ms Sylvia Lim and Ms He Ting Ru spoke about the aspects of diversity, inclusion and mental health – matters cited also by Dr Wan Rizal himself but also Mr Darryl David.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
text: Hence, we fully agree with the need to focus on much more than just sporting achievements by national athletes but also by the rest of us, albeit, we also recognise the inspirational value of marquee events.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
text: NMP Mark Chay critiqued an excessive focus on income as a determiner of sporting success and offered what amounted to an apology for our relative underperformance.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
text: As a national sportsman and a coach, he would be much more familiar with individual sporting challenges.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
text: But I cannot help but wonder if he would be as comfortable if those under his charge not only failed to perform after receiving significant financial support but actually regressed in terms of their sporting performance.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
text: A minor clarification which was a point first raised by Ms Poh Li San but now reiterated by Senior Parliamentary Secretary Chua, which I offered earlier.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
text: Hence, the sentence in my speech referred specifically to the total medal count.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
text: In any case, not to nitpick on such matters of rhetoric, I will go on and speak about areas of improvement.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
text: Both Mr Faisal Manap and Mr Dennis Tan suggested specific improvements to our Youth Development programmes for football, such as ensuring that the coaching and mentoring programmes are on track, not least by making sure that they have a training schedule that meets more than once every half a year and devoting more resources towards lower levels in our grassroots soccer leagues.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
text: In the same spirit, Mr Dennis Tan also suggested barriers to recreational football in our heartlands could be lowered, such as additional funding for sheltered futsal courts, either in open spaces or atop multi-storey car parks.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
text: Melvin Yong also spoke about football and especially stressed the need for dedicated infrastructure and facilities.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
text: Improving the pathways through sporting success for the young was a point made also by Mr Gerald Giam, Ms Poh Li San, Mr Melvin Yong and Dr Wan Rizal.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
text: Ms Poh cited the example of table tennis – one of the sports where Singapore has indeed done relatively well – to argue that private sector efforts are just as important as a complement to the public sector.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
text: Mr Melvin Yong expounded on the range of sporting activities for the youths, especially the Pesta Sukan, where fresh talent may be identified and participation is encouraged.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
text: Mr Gerald Giam, in contrast, suggested expanding the Singapore Sports School which, in turn, would feed into a collegiate sports career.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
text: He also stressed the importance of flexibility for student athletes – a theme that was also made by Mr Leong Mun Wai who spoke about how our young men serve their NS obligations could stand to be relaxed for our top-tier sporting talent.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
text: Mr Gerald Giam also pointed out to how media coverage for local sports could stand to be expanded, making these free-to-air or livestream online.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
text: Final matches, featuring Singaporeans especially, should be broadcast live for all of us to cheer our athletes along.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
text: Mr Leon Perera spoke up for lesser-known sports.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
text: His concrete suggestions include strengthening funding and support for these sports, a sentiment that was also echoed by Dr Wan Rizal.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
text: Mr Perera also spoke of providing state financial support much earlier in the game for our budding athletes, especially to attend tournaments and ensuring sufficient talent in the sports business management field, are all practical ones for beefing up our sports ecosystem.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
text: Ms Sylvia Lim, Ms He Ting Ru and Mr Mark Chay offered ideas for how we can make sport more attractive outside of top-level sporting arenas.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
text: Ms Lim made the case for medical subsidies for national athletes that extend beyond just the time that they are actively representing Singapore, while Ms He stressed that we need to improve inclusivity, especially in our ActiveSG gyms, and Mr Chay stressed the importance of giving regular folks a reason for them to remain active.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
text: Both the Leader of the Opposition Mr Pritam Singh and Mr Leong Mun Wai made appeals that clear and objective criteria be applied to the selection of our national athletes, with both acknowledging that while good conduct is undeniably important, sportsmen and women should not be held to unreasonable standards of behaviour that are not always extended to other public figures.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
text: This helps us avoid unnecessary "own goals" with our already scarce local sporting talent.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
text: On my part, I pointed out that we can use the Sports Hub, the crowning glory of our national sporting scene, as a catalyst and platform to improve community engagement in sports and also called for a re-examination of the efficacy of our current national sport spending.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
text: With regard to achievable goals, let me now attempt to sum up some of the suggestions that have been made by Members of this House over the past hours.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
text: My friend, Mr Faisal Manap, has already articulated: we do not have any definitive answers.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
text: And of course, these goals should eventually be established in consultation with all the stakeholders involved – the athletes and coaches, the NSAs and, of course, Singapore sports fans at large.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
text: It is also unrealistic since we do not have a complete picture of aggregate financial resources that could be credibly committed to these goals.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
text: Hence, the issue is how much more effective can we be with the monies we devote currently already to sport?

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
text: Mr Melvin Yong also suggested that we can benchmark ourselves against successful football nations as a metric for our achievement.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
text: Lesser-known sports can also contribute strongly to our national sporting goals.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
text: Some of these sports have been immensely successful and we can build off their current global rankings and set targets to raise them by a notch or two.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
text: At the very least, it seems appropriate, as Leon Perera has argued, to extend National Sports Association coverage to all sports, including dodgeball and powerlifting, just as they have belatedly done with tchoukball, which I note only occurred this year and does not appear to have been updated on the ActiveSG website, which was the source for our citation.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
text: And in any case, it occurred well after the men and women's teams had already found global success.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
text: Ms Poh Li San pointed to how our existing Government awards, such as the major sports award – the games award programme – play an important role in helping make sports a viable career.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
text: Perhaps we should look to such programmes as only necessary up till through to the medium run and we will hopefully wind these down in the long run, looking instead to a growing local sporting audience to ensure a self-sustaining domestic market for professional athletes to function – much like many other nations, without government grants, relying instead on recognition and sponsorship.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
text: Ms He Ting Ru also provided a clear goal for improving the infrastructure catering to simpler sporting activities like walking and running – our country's most popular sport by far, incidentally, for the non-professional sportsmen and women – to ensure that our "cycle and walk" pass or meet the Government's own design guide specifications islandwide.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
text: She also stressed the need to improve the participation rate in sports among the disabled and others with special needs.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
text: We find the first amendment uncontentious – after all, sporting celebrations or any celebration of accomplishments should always recognise that it stands on the shoulders of those who have come before.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
text: This wiggles, in our view, out of one of the most important fundamentals for sporting performance – appropriately defining success.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
text: It is important to have clarity on what our goals are and ideally set up, not only eventual, but also intermediate targets, that we can credibly achieve.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
text: Accepting the amendment also robs us of being able to meet the sort of mass participation goals that we alluded to that are imminently achievable.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
text: We also doubt that the Government would be comfortable with such ambiguity for other endeavours as a nation, such as where we want our universities to be, or the profitability of our state-owned enterprises.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
text: It will be remiss if I did not close by reiterating my thanks to all our athletes and para-athletes for representing our country.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
text: I know that all of them had to make enormous sacrifices, mentally, emotionally and physically, to be able to compete on the international stage.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
text: You have all carried our flag and done so proudly, and we, in turn, have lived vicariously through you and are immensely proud of all that you have achieved.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
text: But these thanks extend as well to those who have contributed in ways big and small to our local sporting ecosystem: our parents and coaches who are sometimes one and the same; the die-hard and long-suffering supporters and fans; sports announcers, commentators and reporters – they keep us attuned and excited; the administrators and backend support staff for our sporting infrastructure; and also, even down to the maintenance folks who keep it all going: the groundskeepers, stadium cleaners, floodlight technicians, media operators.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
text: Just like how it takes a village to nurture a world-class athlete, in the words of Senior Parliamentary Secretary Chua, it seemingly takes one to keep our current sports system rolling.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
text: Some may ask why the Workers' Party has chosen to speak on this seemingly non-critical issue of sports at this period of time when there appears to be more pressing matters on the horizon – pressures in the cost of living, unaffordable house and car prices and softening economy.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
text: To be clear, we have consistently raised issues of concern and participated in extended debates in this House in these very areas and will continue to do so.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
text: But we are fooling ourselves if we think for a moment that jobs and businesses and the economy constitute the entirety of life.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
text: We work so that we may live, not the other way around.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
text: In this sense, sport captures, in the most general way, both the trade-offs we routinely make in leisure versus labour, that makes life ultimately worth living, while also embodying the measure of our aspirations as a people, a society and a country.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
text: Or in the words of Xie Yao Quan: it reflects our values.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
text: If there is one dimension in life where rankings indisputably matter, it is in sports league tables.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
text: Ultimately, sport is about rowing together, in unison, towards a common goal – the same as nation-building.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
text: Singaporeans have shown by their actions that they, indeed, care about sport.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
text: Perhaps the pandemic gives Singaporeans a taste of the importance of achieving genuine work-life balance.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
text: Perhaps, it was a reminder of our mortality and what we need to do to ensure that we remain fit and healthy.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
text: Or perhaps, it allowed us to reflect on the true value of sports in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Darryl David
text: Assoc Prof Jamus Lim's speech is always interesting because it is peppered with a lot of words, platitudes and so on —

speaker: Mr Darryl David
text: Earlier, Assoc Prof Jamus Lim mentioned the word "wiggly" in reference to one of my proposed amendments.

speaker: Mr Darryl David
text: Again, I do not quite understand what "wiggly" is supposed to mean.

speaker: Mr Darryl David
text: Could I have a clarification from Assoc Prof Jamus Lim?

speaker: Mr Darryl David
text: Perhaps, I could get some clarification on what that actually means, Madam.

speaker: Mdm Deputy Speaker
text: I think it was the point you made on the third amendment.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
text: I said, and this is my exact sentence: "This wiggles out of one of the most important fundamentals for sporting performance." So, I can rephrase this to: "This avoids one of the most important fundamentals for sporting performance." I have been told repeatedly that I should use less bombast in my language and I apologise.

speaker: Mr Darryl David
text: I do not consider "wiggle" a bombastic word at all.

speaker: Mr Darryl David
text: I found it as a word, if I may say and with all due respect, a little bit odd for it to be used in a Parliament setting.

speaker: Mr Darryl David
text: If I may clarify my amendment in the context of the point that was made by Assoc Prof Jamus Lim, Madam, the point I was making was that, when you use the term "sporting success" or success in the context of sports, very often, it is easy to construe that in the context of tangible achievements via winning medals, achieving success in competitions, achieving qualification for major games.

speaker: Mr Darryl David
text: But the point that we have made or we have heard today, indeed, from both sides of the House, is that sport, sporting activities serve multiple purposes.

speaker: Mr Darryl David
text: There are many goals that one can aspire for and aspire to reach.

speaker: Mr Darryl David
text: And while no doubt, one element – and I stress again, just one element – of success in sports would be achievement in games or in competitions or so on.

speaker: Mr Darryl David
text: The very fact that we have agreed that sports play and function in multiple roles in our community, our society, would go to show that it is not just about that word "success", but about achieving our goals with regard to sports.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
text: A quick clarification of the word "success", which I hope is not bombastic.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
text: In no way do I mean "success" to only refer to medals, or even sporting success at the highest levels, like qualifying for some of these international tournaments.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
text: For me, "success" is just being able to meet the goals that one has set.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
text: It may be running a marathon, it may be something like running 2.4 kilometres in 15 minutes.

speaker: Mdm Deputy Speaker
text: We have three amendments proposed by Mr Darryl David.

speaker: Mdm Deputy Speaker
text: Do you want to put up your hands or stand?

speaker: Mdm Deputy Speaker
text: Leader of the Opposition, would you like to register your dissent?

speaker: Mdm Deputy Speaker
text: The amendments have been agreed to, the Original Motion as amended is now before the House.

speaker: Mdm Deputy Speaker
text: Members may wish to stand to register their dissent.
